answerlines: Langston Hughes (or James Mercer Langston Hughes )

clues.text: One poem by this author repeats the line “He did a lazy sway” before describing “ebony hands on each ivory key.”
This poet said "They'll see how beautiful I am / And be ashamed" in a poem that ends by declaring "I, too, am America".
This poet wrote about his travels through Asia, as well as his observations of Haiti and the Soviet Republic in his autobiography, I Wonder as I Wander.

One of his poems is framed as a prompt from a college instructor who said to “Go home and write a page tonight” and mentions the poet’s love for “Bessie, bop, and Bach.”This poet wrote that despite the fact that “they send me to eat in the kitchen,” “I, too, sing America.”
This poet wrote “let it be the dream it used to be” in his poem “Let America be America Again.”
One of his earliest works is a book of poems called The Weary Blues.
Lorraine Hansberry took the title for her play, A Raisin in the Sun, from this man’s poem, “Harlem,” in which he asks, “What happens to a dream deferred?”
This poet of “Theme for English B” proclaimed that it “sags like a heavy load” in a poem that asks “what happens to a dream deferred.”
Name this Harlem Renaissance poet of “Montage of a Dream Deferred”, who describes a dream as “a raisin in the sun” and writes that his soul has grown deep in “The Negro Speaks of Rivers.”
“The Weary Blues” was written by what Harlem Renaissance poet?

answerlines: Nikolai Gogol [Nikolai Vasileyevich Gogol] (The first line clues Piskarev in “Nevsky Prospekt.”)

clues.text: In a story by this author, the narrator signs his forms as Ferdinand VIII (the eighth) after claiming to be heir to the Spanish throne.

One of this author’s short stories begins by describing a “certain official” who “serves in a certain department,” and another contrasts the lives of Lieutenant Pirogov and Piskaryov, who both travel along the title street.
This writer created a puff pastry-eating man who encourages Piskaryov to pursue a beautiful woman he sees on Nevsky Prospekt.
The characters Pirogorov (peer-AHG-uh-rawf) and Piskarev leave each other on the title street in a story by this author.
A character that dresses up as a state councilor is caught leaving for Riga with a fake passport in a story by this author.
In another, two robbers assault the protagonist on his way home from a party celebrating the purchase of the title garment by Akaky Akakievich.
In another story by this writer, the words “I am your brother" make a young official regret making fun of the protagonist, who later confronts the “important person”.
This author’s most prominent work features a character who is rumored to be Napoleon in disguise or the infamous Captain Kopeikin.
The streets of St. Petersburg are haunted by Akaky Akakievich’s spirit in that story by this author.
Name this Russian short-story writer, author of “The Nose” and “The Overcoat.”

answerlines: German [or Deutsch; accept Middle High German] (The first poems mentioned are Novalis’s first and second “Hymns to the Night.” The novel is Heinrich von Ofterdingen by Novalis. The post-power poem is Heine’s “Die Lorelei”)

clues.text: A play written in this language opens with Daja telling the title character how a Christian knight heroically saved his lover Recha from a burning house.
One author who wrote in this language asked “Must the morning always return?” in his poem “Longing for Death” and used a blue flower to symbolize Romanticism.
A famous short poem in this language begins "Above all summits is calm" and ends "just wait, soon you till will rest."
During a play in this language, a character based on a Jewish philosopher tells Saladin a parable about three rings.
This native language of Novalis was used to write one poem pondering “why am I so sad at heart” and centers on a monster who is “combing her golding hair” and “holds a golden comb.”
This language of "Wanderer's Nightsong II" was used for a poem that compares the eyes of the title object to apples ripening and ends "You must change your life."
The title character falls in love with the engaged Charlotte and becomes so miserable he commits suicide in The Sorrows of Young Werther, a work in this language.
The "Anthem of Europe" uses a poem in this language that describes a "spark of divinity" and "daughter of Elysium."
Name this nationality of military officers who have invaded France in stories like "Ball of Fat" by Guy de Maupassant.
Name this language of playwright Bertolt Brecht.
